results.title: The signature of the small intestinal epithelial and immune ...
results.content: The human gut is home to a vast array of microorganisms, forming a complex and intimate relationship with their host.[10–12] Gut commensal microbiota play a crucial role in numerous physiological processes and in maintaining intestinal immune homeostasis.[13–15] They robustly contribute to the host’s defense system by promoting the maturation of the intestinal mucosal immune system and resistance to pathogenic microbial invasion.[13] IECs serve as a key arm in maintaining intestinal immune homeostasis[16] and protecting against enteric pathogens[17] by providing a physical barrier and secreting various antimicrobial factors, including AMPs. Among these, Paneth cells are one of the primary sources of AMPs.[18] Located at the crypt base in the small intestine, Paneth cells are distinguished by their large granules filled with AMPs and signaling molecules.
